title: [RPG Design Guides] Scenario Design with Gameplay in Mind

blocks.source: 【RPG制作講座】ゲーム性を意識したシナリオ
blocks.translation: [RPG Design Guides] Scenario Design with Gameplay in Mind

blocks.source: 小説、映画、漫画、アニメ……ストーリー性を持った媒体は様々に存在するが、ゲームもその一つである。
blocks.translation: Novels, films, manga, anime... There are many forms of media with stories, and games are one of them.

blocks.source: ゲームにもＲＰＧ、シミュレーション、アクション、ＡＤＶというように様々なジャンルが存在する。
blocks.translation: Games also come in many genres, such as RPGs, simulations, action games, and ADV games.

blocks.source: シナリオは媒体やジャンルによって、最適なものを書く必要がある。
blocks.translation: A scenario needs to be tailored to its medium and genre.

blocks.source: というわけで、ＲＰＧのゲーム性を意識した上で、どのようなシナリオを書けばよいかを考えてみたい。
blocks.translation: With that in mind, I would like to consider what kind of scenario to write while keeping the gameplay of an RPG in mind.

blocks.source: 逆に「シナリオを活かすために、どのようなシステムを用意すればいいか」という観点もいくつか書いている。
blocks.translation: Conversely, I have also written about what kinds of systems should be prepared to make the most of a scenario.

blocks.source: 筆者は個人制作者なので、もちろんゲームデザイナー兼シナリオライターという立場である。
blocks.translation: As an independent creator, I naturally fill the roles of both game designer and scenario writer.

blocks.source: 現代のプロのゲームクリエイターは専門化されていて、両方に精通している人は希少らしい。なので、両方をやっている人間でしか得られない観点を出せればと思っている。
blocks.translation: Modern professional game creators tend to specialize, and apparently it is rare to find someone well versed in both areas. I hope to offer perspectives that can only be gained by someone who does both.

blocks.source: そのまま個人制作で活かしてもいいし。ゲームデザイナーとシナリオライターで分業する時の注意点として活かしてもよいかと思う。
blocks.translation: You can apply these ideas directly to your own solo projects, or use them as points to keep in mind when dividing the work between a game designer and a scenario writer.

blocks.source: なお、過去にも以下のような記事を書いているが、今回はより詳細に掘り下げている。
blocks.translation: I have written articles like the following in the past, but this time I delve into the subject in greater detail.

blocks.source: 媒体としてのRPGを考えてみる
blocks.translation: Considering RPGs as a Medium

blocks.source: https://newrpg.seesaa.net/article/367906483.html
blocks.translation: https://newrpg.seesaa.net/article/367906483.html

blocks.source: 目次
blocks.translation: Table of Contents

blocks.source: 仲間の存在
blocks.translation: The Presence of Companions

blocks.source: ＲＰＧのシナリオを考える上で、まず大事なのは仲間の存在である。
blocks.translation: When considering an RPG scenario, the first important thing is the presence of companions.

blocks.source: 多くのＲＰＧでは主人公は数多くの仲間を引き連れて、冒険することになる。
blocks.translation: In many RPGs, the protagonist goes on adventures accompanied by numerous companions.

blocks.source: 仲間はプレイヤーにとって、ゲームシステム上の駒である。だが、そこにストーリー性が紐づけば、仲間は単なる駒を超えた存在にもなる。
blocks.translation: To the player, companions are pieces within the game system. However, when they are tied to the story, they can become more than mere pieces.

blocks.source: 魅力的な仲間達を操作できるということは、ＲＰＧの大きな魅力だ。これを活かさない手はない。
blocks.translation: Being able to control appealing companions is one of the great attractions of RPGs. There is no reason not to make use of it.

blocks.source: 仲間の加入
blocks.translation: Joining the Party

blocks.source: 仲間の加入はストーリー的にもゲーム的にも、大きな見所となる。魅力的なキャラクターが仲間になった時は、プレイヤーにとっても強い喜びとなるはず。
blocks.translation: A companion joining the party is a major highlight, both in terms of the story and the gameplay. When an appealing character joins the party, it should bring the player great joy as well.

blocks.source: さらには、加入した仲間が戦闘でも大活躍できる性能だった時は、大いに盛り上がるだろう。
blocks.translation: Furthermore, if the new companion proves highly effective in battle, it will make the experience even more exciting.

blocks.source: そんなわけで、ゲーム序盤は仲間の加入イベントを用意するのがセオリーとなる。
blocks.translation: For this reason, preparing companion recruitment events early in the game is standard practice.

blocks.source: ヒロインとの運命の出会いや、頼りになる相棒との出会いを、華々しく演出しよう。
blocks.translation: Dramatically portray the fateful meeting with the heroine or the encounter with a dependable partner.

blocks.source: 活躍機会を与えるためにも、仲間の加入は遅すぎないほうが望ましい。中盤ぐらいまでには、大半のキャラを仲間にできるぐらいが目安だろうか。
blocks.translation: To give companions opportunities to shine, it is preferable not to have them join too late. A good guideline might be to have most of the characters available by around the midpoint.

blocks.source: 特に注意したいのは序盤の仲間の加入だ。
blocks.translation: The companions who join early in the game require particular attention.

blocks.source: 多くのＲＰＧでは一人旅を含めた少人数では、取れる戦術が限られてしまう。
blocks.translation: In many RPGs, when the party is small, including when traveling alone, the tactics available to the player become limited.

blocks.source: その中でも、回復役がいない状況がずっと続くのは厳しい。回復役は比較的、早めに加入させておこう。ドラクエシリーズのように、主人公にある程度の回復技を覚えさせておくのもセオリーの一つだ。
blocks.translation: In particular, it is difficult if the party goes too long without a healer. Have a healer join relatively early. Another standard approach, as seen in the Dragon Quest series, is to have the protagonist learn some healing Techs.

blocks.source: なお、ポケモンのように回復技を前提としたゲームバランスになっていない作品はこの限りではない。
blocks.translation: This does not apply to games such as Pokémon, whose game balance is not built around the use of healing Techs.

blocks.source: その他の仲間についても、ゲーム性に合わせて調整したい。
blocks.translation: The other companions should also be adjusted to fit the gameplay.

blocks.source: 例えば、通常攻撃しかできない少人数の旅がずっと続いてしまうと、プレイヤーも退屈に感じてしまう。早めに魔法など戦術の広がるスキルを持った仲間を加入させてあげよう。
blocks.translation: For example, if the player spends too long traveling with a small party that can only use normal attacks, they will become bored. Have a companion with skills that expand their tactical options, such as magic, join early on.

blocks.source: 仲間は徐々に増やす
blocks.translation: Increase the Number of Companions Gradually

blocks.source: ならば、冒頭から大勢の仲間を加入させてはどうか？
blocks.translation: In that case, why not have a large number of companions join right from the beginning?

blocks.source: ……と、思うかもしれないが、そちらも避けたほうが無難だろう。
blocks.translation: You might think so, but it would probably be safer to avoid that as well.

blocks.source: というのも、一人一人に焦点を当てる機会が減るので、プレイヤーがキャラクターを把握しづらくなる。
blocks.translation: The reason is that there will be fewer opportunities to focus on each individual, making it harder for players to get to know the characters.

blocks.source: また、システム的にもいきなり大勢の仲間を管理する必要が出るので、慣れない内からプレイヤーの負担が大きくなってしまう。
blocks.translation: From a systems perspective, the player would also suddenly have to manage a large number of companions, increasing the burden before they have had time to get used to the game.

blocks.source: 単純にストーリーのネタが減ってしまうのも厳しい。仲間の登場と加入のイベントはそれだけで強い牽引力があるので、活用しないのはもったいないと思う。
blocks.translation: It is also difficult simply because it reduces the amount of story material available. Events involving the appearance and recruitment of companions are powerful hooks in themselves, so I think it would be a waste not to use them.

blocks.source: もっとも、この辺は作品の狙いによって様々なやり方があるので、柔軟に考えて欲しい。
blocks.translation: That said, there are many possible approaches depending on the goals of the work, so I hope you will think flexibly.

blocks.source: 例えば、冒頭からいきなり多人数パーティにした代わりに、徐々に仲間を掘り下げていくというスタイルもある。
blocks.translation: For example, one possible style is to start with a large party and gradually delve deeper into each companion instead.

blocks.source: 成長システムとの兼ね合い
blocks.translation: Balancing the Growth System

blocks.source: 成長・強化システムと仲間の加入・離脱には相性がある。ストーリーを作成する上で無視できない部分だ。
blocks.translation: Growth and enhancement systems have a natural compatibility with companions joining and leaving the party. This is an aspect that cannot be ignored when creating a story.

blocks.source: これについては、過去の記事でも詳しく書いている。
blocks.translation: I wrote about this in detail in a previous article as well.

blocks.source: パーティ編成による分類
blocks.translation: Classifying Characters by Party Formation

blocks.source: https://newrpg.seesaa.net/article/302353840.html
blocks.translation: https://newrpg.seesaa.net/article/302353840.html

blocks.source: 例えば、ドラクエ６～７の職業システムが有名だろう。
blocks.translation: For example, the class systems in Dragon Quest VI and VII are probably well known.

blocks.source: 両作品の職業は戦闘回数によって、呪文・特技を習得するようになっている。
blocks.translation: In both games, characters learn spells and Techs for their classes based on the number of battles fought.

blocks.source: 後半、仲間になったキャラは職業の初期レベルが固定になっており、扱いづらくなってしまう。
blocks.translation: Characters who join later in the game have fixed starting levels for their classes, which makes them more difficult to use.

blocks.source: また、レベルアップボーナスのようなシステムがある作品だと、後半に高レベルで仲間になるキャラは不利を受けてしまいがち。
blocks.translation: Also, in games with systems such as level-up bonuses, characters who join at high levels later in the game tend to be disadvantaged.

blocks.source: このようなシステムはそもそも採用しないほうが無難だろう。
blocks.translation: It would probably be safer not to use such a system in the first place.

blocks.source: 逆に言うと昔のドラクエのように、レベルと装備だけで能力が決まるような単純な設計ならば、加入時期は遅くとも大きな問題は起きない。
blocks.translation: Conversely, with a simple design like that of the older Dragon Quest games, where abilities are determined solely by level and equipment, having a character join late does not cause any major problems.

blocks.source: あるいはドラクエ８や１１のように、ポイント振り分け型のシステムも問題は起きにくい。仲間になってから自由にポイントを振り分けられるようにしておけばいいだろう。
blocks.translation: Alternatively, point-allocation systems like those in Dragon Quest VIII and XI are also less likely to cause problems. You can simply allow players to freely allocate points after a character joins.

blocks.source: ただし、あまりにも振り分けに時間がかかるようなシステムだと、プレイヤーの手間が増えてしまうことには注意したい。
blocks.translation: However, keep in mind that if the system takes too much time to allocate points, it will increase the player's workload.

blocks.source: 仲間の離脱
blocks.translation: Leaving the Party

blocks.source: ストーリー上の都合で、頻繁にパーティ編成を変えてしまうと、結果的にシステムを十分に体験できなくなってしまう。（ＦＦ１３の前半など）
blocks.translation: When the party lineup is changed frequently for story-related reasons, the player ultimately cannot fully experience the system (as in the first half of FF XIII, for example).

blocks.source: さらに厳しいのは仲間の永久離脱だ。
blocks.translation: Even harsher is when companions leave the party permanently.

blocks.source: 成長システムが凝ったものになればなるほど、仲間の離脱は好まれなくなる。せっかく手間をかけて育てたのにストーリーの都合で離脱されてしまっては、腹立たしくもなるというもの。
blocks.translation: The more elaborate the growth system becomes, the less welcome it is for companions to leave. After taking the trouble to raise someone, it is only natural to feel frustrated when they leave for story-related reasons.

blocks.source: こういった作品の場合は、ゲームシステムの段階でフォローをしておきたい。
blocks.translation: For works like these, I want the game system itself to provide some support.

blocks.source: ＦＦ５では離脱した仲間の能力を引き継いだ後継キャラが加入する。
blocks.translation: In FF V, a successor character who inherits the abilities of a departed companion joins the party.

blocks.source: ＦＦ７ではマテリアシステムによって、モノを成長させる仕様になっており、離脱による戦力低下が痛手にならないようになっている。
blocks.translation: In FF VII, the Materia system is designed around developing items, so the loss of combat power caused by a companion's departure is less painful.

blocks.source: 仲間の人数
blocks.translation: Number of Companions

blocks.source: 仲間の人数が多い作品は、単純に管理の手間が増えるため、複雑な成長・強化システムとの相性が悪い。
blocks.translation: Works with many companions are a poor match for complex growth and enhancement systems, simply because they require more effort to manage.

blocks.source: 例えば、軌跡シリーズには数十人という膨大な仲間が登場する作品もある。それらがストーリー展開によって加入・離脱するのだが、その度に多数の装備を組み直さないといけないようになっている。
blocks.translation: For example, some entries in the Trails series feature a huge number of companions—dozens of them. They join and leave according to the story, and each time, you have to rearrange a large number of pieces of equipment.

blocks.source: 場合によっては、パーティ分割ダンジョンなどで１２人以上の装備を整える必要があったりするが、これはプレイヤーにとって無視できないストレスになる。
blocks.translation: In some cases, such as dungeons that split the party, you may need to prepare equipment for more than twelve characters. This creates a level of stress that players cannot simply ignore.

blocks.source: 仲間になる人数が多い作品でも、戦闘に参加する人数が少なく、限られたキャラだけを整えればいいなら手間は軽減できる。
blocks.translation: Even in works with many recruitable companions, the burden can be reduced if only a small number participate in battle and you only need to prepare a limited selection of characters.

blocks.source: 無理に大勢の仲間を使わせるようなストーリーおよびシステムを作ると、それだけ手間がかかることは気をつけておきたい。
blocks.translation: Keep in mind that creating a story and system that force players to use a large number of companions will require a corresponding amount of extra work.

blocks.source: かわいい子には旅を
blocks.translation: Send Your Beloved Child on a Journey

blocks.source: 仲間として旅に参加するキャラクターは、ゲーム的にもシナリオ的にも出番がとても多くなる。
blocks.translation: Characters who join the journey as companions get far more screen time, both in terms of gameplay and the story.

blocks.source: 故郷で主人公の帰りを待つヒロインと、主人公と共に戦うヒロインならば、後者のほうが圧倒的に愛着が湧くはずだ。
blocks.translation: Between a heroine who waits in her hometown for the protagonist to return and one who fights alongside the protagonist, the latter will surely inspire far more attachment.

blocks.source: 漫画やアニメ、ＡＤＶならば、「戦士として敵と戦う主人公」の裏で「王女として政治に奔走するヒロイン」を描いても十分に魅力を出せるだろうけれど、ＲＰＧにおいてはこれも厳しい。
blocks.translation: In manga, anime, or an ADV, you could make a heroine who busies herself with politics as a princess plenty appealing while the protagonist fights enemies as a warrior. In an RPG, however, this is also difficult.

blocks.source: ＲＰＧでは、プレイ時間の大半が主人公の周辺の出来事として描かれるためだ。特に戦闘や探索の占める割合は大きい。
blocks.translation: That is because most of an RPG's playtime depicts events taking place around the protagonist. Combat and exploration, in particular, make up a large portion of it.

blocks.source: それらの際に、主人公に同行していないヒロインは圧倒的に描写が不足してしまう。同行するヒロインと比較して、プレイヤーの目に触れる時間に１００倍以上の差がつくことすらある。
blocks.translation: During those parts, a heroine who does not accompany the protagonist ends up being dramatically underrepresented. Compared with an accompanying heroine, the difference in the amount of time players see her can even exceed a hundredfold.

blocks.source: ヒロインは主人公の幼馴染で小さい頃からずっと仲良くしていた――なんて説明をされたところで、プレイヤーはその体験を共有していないのだから仕方ない。
blocks.translation: You can explain that the heroine is the protagonist's childhood friend and that they have been close since they were young—but the player did not share those experiences, so there is only so much that can be done.

blocks.source: ヒロインを例に挙げたけど、他のキャラクターも同様である。
blocks.translation: I used the heroine as an example, but the same applies to other characters.

blocks.source: 敵キャラならば、実際に何度も戦って苦戦した相手のほうが印象も強くなる。
blocks.translation: For an enemy, one that players have actually fought repeatedly and struggled against will leave a much stronger impression.

blocks.source: キャラクターの印象を強くしたいなら、ゲームシステム上の出番を用意してあげよう。
blocks.translation: If you want to make a character more memorable, give them opportunities to appear through the game system.

blocks.source: 戦闘
blocks.translation: Combat

blocks.source: 一般的なＲＰＧでは戦闘がゲーム性の肝になる。
blocks.translation: In a typical RPG, combat is the core of the gameplay.

blocks.source: ＲＰＧのゲーム性とは事実上戦闘であり、それを意識せずしてストーリーは作れない。必然的に、ストーリーも戦闘を意識したものにする必要がある。
blocks.translation: In practice, an RPG's gameplay is combat, and it is impossible to create a story without taking that into account. Inevitably, the story must also be designed with combat in mind.

blocks.source: ※戦闘のないＲＰＧのようなごくわずかの例外もありますが、今回は置いておきます。
blocks.translation: ※There are a very few exceptions, such as RPGs without combat, but we will set those aside for now.

blocks.source: ストーリーとゲーム性の一致
blocks.translation: Aligning the Story with the Gameplay

blocks.source: 例えば、戦いを否定する平和主義的なストーリーを作りたいとしよう。主人公やヒロインはひたすら暴力を否定し、敵との対話を模索し続ける。
blocks.translation: For example, suppose you want to create a pacifist story that rejects fighting. The protagonist and heroine relentlessly denounce violence and continue seeking dialogue with their enemies.

blocks.source: このようなストーリーのコンセプトと、ひたすら敵を倒すことを要求するゲームシステムとの相性の悪さは直感的に分かると思う。
blocks.translation: I think it is intuitively clear that this story concept is a poor match for a game system that relentlessly demands that players defeat enemies.

blocks.source: 綺麗事を言っていても、結局は戦闘で物事を解決するならば、どこか偽善的な印象をプレイヤーに与えてしまうだろう。
blocks.translation: Even if the characters talk about lofty ideals, if they ultimately solve everything through combat, players will be left with a somewhat hypocritical impression.

blocks.source: ならば――と、戦闘の回避を推奨するようなシステムを導入してしまうと、今度は戦闘システムを作り込む意義がなくなってしまう。
blocks.translation: You might then introduce a system that encourages avoiding combat, but that would eliminate the point of creating an elaborate combat system in the first place.

blocks.source: そんなわけで、オーソドックスにＲＰＧを作るならば、ストーリーは戦いを前提にすることが無難だろう。
blocks.translation: Therefore, if you are making a conventional RPG, it is probably safest for the story to be built around conflict.

blocks.source: ボス戦を意識する
blocks.translation: Keep Boss Battles in Mind

blocks.source: 多くのＲＰＧではボスを倒すことが物語の目的に直結している。
blocks.translation: In many RPGs, defeating the boss is directly tied to the story's objective.

blocks.source: ボスには中ボスからラスボスまで色々とあるが、ボス戦こそがＲＰＧの華だと言ってもよいだろう。
blocks.translation: There are various kinds of bosses, from mid-bosses to the final boss, but it would not be an exaggeration to say that boss battles are the highlight of an RPG.

blocks.source: 従って、ＲＰＧのストーリーもボス戦を意識して作成することが望ましい。
blocks.translation: Accordingly, it is best to create an RPG story with boss battles in mind.

blocks.source: そのためにも、必要なのは魅力的な敵キャラだ。
blocks.translation: To that end, what you need are compelling enemies.

blocks.source: 非道な悪党でも、悲劇の悪役でも、正々堂々としたライバルでもいい。魅力の出し方は様々である。
blocks.translation: They can be a ruthless villain, a tragic antagonist, or an honorable rival. There are many ways to make an enemy compelling.

blocks.source: ベタではあるが『四天王』のような敵幹部を用意するのも王道だ。
blocks.translation: It may be a cliché, but creating a group of enemy commanders like the Four Heavenly Kings is also a classic approach.

blocks.source: 敵キャラには出番と対決の機会が欠かせない。顔見せ的なイベントを作ったり、複数回の対決機会を設けたりして、印象を強めていこう。
blocks.translation: Enemies need opportunities to appear and chances to face the player. Create introductory events, provide multiple opportunities for confrontation, and work to make them more memorable.

blocks.source: こういったストーリー上の宿敵との激戦は、ゲームでしか得られない熱さがある。
blocks.translation: Fierce battles against story-defining nemeses like these have an intensity that can only be experienced in a game.

blocks.source: ありがちなのは、各エリアの最後にその場限りのボスが現れるばかりというパターン。そうならないように、敵キャラはしっかり意識して描こう。
blocks.translation: A common pattern is for a disposable boss to appear at the end of each area and nowhere else. To avoid that, give careful thought to how you portray your enemies.

blocks.source: プレイヤーの操作を尊重しよう
blocks.translation: Respect the Player's Input

blocks.source: ゲームである以上、プレイヤーが操作する戦闘は大切であり、尊重しなければならない。ストーリーの都合でプレイヤーの操作をないがしろにするような展開は、なるべく避けたいところだ。
blocks.translation: Since this is a game, the combat controlled by the player is important and must be respected. It is best to avoid developments that disregard the player's input for the sake of the story.

blocks.source: 決着のつかないボス戦
blocks.translation: Boss Battles Without Resolution

blocks.source: プレイヤーが戦闘でボスを倒しても、ボスがピンピンしてるパターン。
blocks.translation: This is the pattern where the player defeats a boss in battle, yet the boss is still perfectly fine.

blocks.source: 「なかなかやるな。今日はここまでにしよう」などと宣って、ボスは颯爽と去っていく。閃の軌跡などで散々に見せられた一幕だ。
blocks.translation: The boss declares something like, “Not bad. Let's call it a day,” then makes a dramatic exit. It is a scene we have seen countless times in works such as Trails of Cold Steel.

blocks.source: 一度の戦闘だけで決着をつけてしまうと、敵キャラの掘り下げができないため、ある程度は仕方ない。
blocks.translation: It is somewhat unavoidable, since resolving everything in a single battle would leave no opportunity to develop the enemy character.

blocks.source: とはいえ、このような展開は「プレイヤーが勝利した」という達成感を損ねてしまう。こういった展開があまりにも多すぎると、戦闘がどんどん茶番じみていくため、プレイヤーもあまり気分はよくないはず。
blocks.translation: Even so, developments like these undermine the feeling of accomplishment that comes from “the player achieving victory.” If this happens too often, battles increasingly start to feel like a farce, which is unlikely to leave players feeling good.

blocks.source: イベントシーンによる戦闘
blocks.translation: Combat Through Event Scenes

blocks.source: ゼノブレイド２～３では、プレイヤーが介入できない戦闘ムービーが非常に多い。
blocks.translation: In Xenoblade Chronicles 2 and 3, there are an enormous number of battle cutscenes in which the player cannot intervene.

blocks.source: プレイヤーが戦闘でボスを倒したのにも関わらず、それがなかったかのように長い戦闘ムービーが挟まれる。通常の戦闘画面では不可能な派手な演出で、敵との決着を大いに盛り上げる。
blocks.translation: Even when the player has defeated a boss in battle, a lengthy battle cutscene is inserted as if that had never happened. With flashy effects impossible to achieve on the regular battle screen, these scenes greatly heighten the excitement of the enemy's defeat.

blocks.source: ……が、その一方で、プレイヤーの操作する戦闘は、シーンの合間に挟まれるミニゲームの如き有様である。個人的には「プレイヤーの操作はいらなくね？」「アニメでも見たほうがよくない？」という印象すら受けてしまった。
blocks.translation: ...On the other hand, the battles controlled by the player are like minigames inserted between scenes. Personally, they even left me thinking, “Do we really need player input?” and “Wouldn’t it be better to just watch an anime?”

blocks.source: こういった問題は戦闘とムービーの落差を小さくすれば、ある程度は違和感を抑えられるかと思う。例えば、戦闘の延長であるかのように決着演出を実行すればよい。
blocks.translation: I think these issues can be made less jarring by reducing the gap between battles and cutscenes to some extent. For example, the finishing sequence could be presented as an extension of the battle.

blocks.source: イベントバトルの功罪
blocks.translation: The Merits and Demerits of Event Battles

blocks.source: 強制敗北戦闘や強制勝利戦闘といったイベントバトルは、ＲＰＧの定番である。
blocks.translation: Event battles, such as forced-loss battles and forced-win battles, are staples of RPGs.

blocks.source: 例えば、圧倒的な強さを持ったボスに強制敗北させることで、将来の再戦への期待を持たせることができる。
blocks.translation: For example, forcing the player to lose to an overwhelmingly powerful boss can build anticipation for a rematch in the future.

blocks.source: ドラクエ５における少年期の最後のシーンは有名だが、強く印象に残った人も多いだろう。
blocks.translation: The final scene of the childhood arc in Dragon Quest V is famous, and many people probably remember it vividly.

blocks.source: 一方でデメリットもある。イベントバトルは原則、プレイヤーの操作によって結果を覆せない。
blocks.translation: On the other hand, there are drawbacks as well. In principle, the outcome of an event battle cannot be overturned through the player's actions.

blocks.source: プレイヤーがどんなにキャラを鍛えて的確な操作をしても、意味がないということでもある。その点では、あまり喜ばしいものではないだろう。
blocks.translation: In other words, no matter how much the player trains their characters or how skillfully they play, it makes no difference. From that perspective, they are not exactly something to celebrate.

blocks.source: ※一応、ある程度ダメージを与えないとゲームオーバーになるといった調整にすることでゲーム性を付与できるが、負けたという印象は残る。
blocks.translation: ※It is possible to add some gameplay by making adjustments such as triggering a Game Over unless the player deals a certain amount of damage, but the impression of having lost remains.

blocks.source: 個人的に気になったのはＦＦ９。
blocks.translation: The one that personally caught my attention was Final Fantasy IX.

blocks.source: この作品では、ストーリーの山場を三度に渡って強制敗北戦闘で潰している。しかも、相手はタダの人間なので、わざわざ何度も強制敗北させる理由はよく分からない。
blocks.translation: In this game, three story climaxes are undermined by forced-loss battles. What is more, the opponents are merely human, so I do not really understand why the player is made to lose repeatedly.

blocks.source: ＦＦ９ではこのせいもあって、ストーリーの高さに反して盛り上がるボス戦が少なくなっている。非常にもったいないように思う。
blocks.translation: In Final Fantasy IX, this also contributes to there being fewer exciting boss battles despite the strength of its story. It seems like a terrible waste.

blocks.source: そんなわけで、強制敗北を使うにしても乱用は避けたいところだ。
blocks.translation: For that reason, even when using forced losses, it is best to avoid overusing them.

blocks.source: なお、強制勝利戦闘も「やらされている感」という点では同じだが、こちらを多用する作品はあまり見ないので問題になることは少ない。
blocks.translation: Forced-win battles also give the same feeling of “being made to do it,” but relatively few games make heavy use of them, so they are less likely to become a problem.

blocks.source: ストーリー進行
blocks.translation: Story Progression

blocks.source: ゲームの特徴は双方向性があること――つまり、プレイヤーが操作できることである。そのため、ストーリーもそれを意識したものを作りたい。
blocks.translation: A defining feature of games is interactivity—in other words, the fact that players can control them. Therefore, I want to create stories with that in mind as well.

blocks.source: ＡＤＶのようなジャンルならば、ゲーム性を重視しない作りにしてしまうのも一つの手ではあるが、この記事ではあくまでゲーム性との両立を目指したシナリオを考えていきたい。
blocks.translation: For a genre such as an ADV, one option would be to design it without emphasizing gameplay, but in this article I want to consider scenarios that aim to balance story and gameplay.

blocks.source: ゲームテンポを殺さない
blocks.translation: Do Not Kill the Game's Pace

blocks.source: イベントがあまりにも長すぎると、ゲームのテンポを削いでしまう。
blocks.translation: If events are too long, they undermine the game's pace.

blocks.source: 極端なものになると、ゲームをやっているというより動画を見ていると揶揄される作品（いわゆるムービーゲーなど）まである。
blocks.translation: At the extreme, some games are even mocked as being more like watching a video than playing a game (so-called “movie games”).

blocks.source: ＳＦＣ時代のドラクエ５やＦＦ５～６を改めてプレイすると、ストーリー性は高いのにセリフが簡潔なことに驚く。
blocks.translation: When I replayed Dragon Quest V and Final Fantasy V and VI from the SNES era, I was surprised by how concise the dialogue was despite their strong storytelling.

blocks.source: 容量の制約という事情もあって、削れるところをバッサリと削った結果かもしれないが、個人的には一つの理想系だと思っている。
blocks.translation: This may have been the result of cutting away anything that could be removed due to storage limitations, but personally, I consider it one ideal approach.

blocks.source: そこまで思い切るのは難しいにしても、セリフを簡潔にしたり、適時プレイヤーの操作を挟むことによって、ゲームテンポを損なわないようにしたい。
blocks.translation: Even if it is difficult to be quite that ruthless, I want to preserve the game's pace by keeping dialogue concise and inserting player input at appropriate times.

blocks.source: ただし、プレイヤーの操作を挟むにしても、『フラグ立て』や『たらい回し』が多いとそれはそれで問題だ。「あっちへ行け」「こっちへ行け」と延々と本題に入らないようではストレスになってしまう。
blocks.translation: However, even when inserting player input, having too much “flag setting” and “being sent back and forth” can create problems of its own. It becomes frustrating if the game keeps saying “Go over there” and “Go over here” without ever getting to the point.

blocks.source: 短いイベントなら、場面転換を挟みながらサクッとまとめてしまってもよいだろう。
blocks.translation: For a short event, it may be fine to wrap things up briskly while using scene transitions.

blocks.source: コツはそもそも、ストーリーを複雑化しすぎないこと。
blocks.translation: The key is not to make the story overly complicated in the first place.

blocks.source: ストーリーを複雑にすればするほど、プレイヤーに対して必要な説明は増えていくので、こういった問題も増えていく。
blocks.translation: The more complicated the story becomes, the more explanation the player needs, which leads to more of these problems.

blocks.source: 時にはバッサリ切り捨てる決断も必要だ。
blocks.translation: Sometimes, you need to make the decision to cut things out completely.

blocks.source: メッセージ表示は快適に
blocks.translation: Make Message Display Comfortable

blocks.source: あまり指摘されることは少ないけれど、メッセージ表示のシステム周りは大事にしたい。
blocks.translation: It is not often pointed out, but I want to pay close attention to the systems surrounding message display.

blocks.source: メッセージ表示が遅かったり、立ち絵を表示する度に時間がかかったりする作品は、それだけでかなりテンポが悪く感じられる。文字が小さかったり、横長のメッセージウィンドウいっぱいに表示するのも非常に読みづらい。
blocks.translation: Games with slow message display or long delays whenever character portraits appear feel sluggish all on their own. Small text, or text that fills an entire wide message window, is also extremely difficult to read.

blocks.source: さらに酷い例になると、白っぽいウィンドウに白文字（さすがに黒縁つき）という嫌がらせのようなものすらある。
blocks.translation: In even worse cases, there are things that seem almost deliberately hostile, such as white text (at least with a black outline) displayed in a whitish window.

blocks.source: ＲＰＧにおいて文章を読む時間はとても長いので、しっかりと注意を払っておこう。
blocks.translation: Since players spend a very long time reading text in RPGs, be sure to give this careful attention.

blocks.source: ダンジョン
blocks.translation: Dungeons

blocks.source: ＲＰＧに欠かせない要素としてダンジョンの存在がある。
blocks.translation: Dungeons are an essential element of RPGs.

blocks.source: ダンジョンに潜り、大勢の雑魚敵を倒しながら、奥のボスを倒すことが毎度の目的になっているＲＰＧは数多い。
blocks.translation: Many RPGs make it their recurring objective to venture into a dungeon, defeat large numbers of weak enemies, and defeat the boss at the end.

blocks.source: ストーリーを考える上で、どのようなダンジョンを登場させるかも考えておこう。
blocks.translation: When considering the story, you should also think about what kinds of dungeons to include.

blocks.source: ひたすら洞窟ばかりではなく、バリエーションを確保したいところだ。ストーリーの山場ならば、それにふさわしいダンジョンが欲しい。
blocks.translation: Rather than relying solely on caves, you should aim for variety. If it is a story climax, you want a dungeon worthy of the occasion.

blocks.source: これについても過去に考察している。
blocks.translation: I have also examined this topic in the past.

blocks.source: ダンジョンバランス① 面白いダンジョンとは？
blocks.translation: Dungeon Balance 1: What Makes a Dungeon Fun?

blocks.source: https://newrpg.seesaa.net/article/210530419.html
blocks.translation: https://newrpg.seesaa.net/article/210530419.html

blocks.source: 町人を活用しよう
blocks.translation: Make Use of Townspeople

blocks.source: ゲームシナリオの特徴は双方向性だと既に述べたが、その中には「読んでも読まなくてもよい」という自由度も含まれている。
blocks.translation: I have already mentioned that interactivity is a defining feature of game scenarios, and this includes the freedom to choose whether or not to read something.

blocks.source: 特に一般的なのは町人の存在だろう。
blocks.translation: The most common example is probably the presence of townspeople.

blocks.source: 町人に話しかけるかどうかは、プレイヤーの判断に委ねられている。
blocks.translation: Whether to talk to a towns person is left up to the player's judgment.

blocks.source: 古いＲＰＧでは、町人に話しかけないと次の行き先も分からないような作品も多かった。現在ではメインストーリー上で常に行き先を明示するのが一般的である。
blocks.translation: In many older RPGs, players could not even learn where to go next unless they talked to the townspeople. Today, it is standard for the main story to always make the next destination clear.

blocks.source: ともあれ、現在のＲＰＧでも町人は有効活用していきたい。
blocks.translation: Even so, townspeople should still be put to good use in modern RPGs.

blocks.source: 例えば、メインストーリーで垂れ流すと冗長になってしまうような細かい説明を、町人に任せてしまおう。
blocks.translation: For example, let townspeople handle the detailed explanations that would become unnecessarily verbose if they were delivered nonstop in the main story.

blocks.source: このようにすれば、テンポよくゲームを進めたいプレイヤーと、じっくり文章を読みたいプレイヤーへのアプローチを両立できる。
blocks.translation: This allows you to accommodate both players who want to progress through the game at a brisk pace and those who want to take their time reading the text.

blocks.source: なお、過去に以下の記事を書いている。
blocks.translation: I have also written the following articles in the past.

blocks.source: 町人のセリフ・配置
blocks.translation: Townspeople’s Dialogue and Placement

blocks.source: https://newrpg.seesaa.net/article/383233037.html
blocks.translation: https://newrpg.seesaa.net/article/383233037.html

blocks.source: 仲間との任意会話
blocks.translation: Optional Conversations with Party Members

blocks.source: ここでいう『仲間との任意会話』とは、ドラクエシリーズのように仲間と会話するシステムを指している。
blocks.translation: By “optional conversations with party members,” I mean a system for talking with party members, like in the Dragon Quest series.

blocks.source: ドラクエのようにメニュー画面から呼び出せてもいいし、拠点や酒場、ダンジョン内の安全地帯などで話しかけられるようにしてもいい。
blocks.translation: You could allow these conversations to be called up from the menu, as in Dragon Quest, or let players talk to party members at bases, in taverns, or in safe areas within dungeons.

blocks.source: 扱いとしては上述の町人との会話と同じだが、仲間の存在感を高めることができる。目指す方向によっては採用してみよう。
blocks.translation: They would be handled in the same way as conversations with townspeople described above, but they can help give party members a stronger presence. Consider adopting this approach depending on what you are aiming for.

blocks.source: 自由度
blocks.translation: Freedom of Choice

blocks.source: ゲームには自由度があるので、それに沿ったストーリーを作ることもできる。
blocks.translation: Games offer freedom of choice, so you can also create a story that takes advantage of it.

blocks.source: 選択肢によるストーリー分岐や、攻略が任意のサブクエストなどが代表的だろう。あるいは仲間との恋愛要素を設ける作品もある。
blocks.translation: Story branches based on choices and optional side quests are typical examples. Some games also include romantic elements involving party members.

blocks.source: これについては、過去に以下の記事を書いている。
blocks.translation: I have written the following article about this in the past.

blocks.source: 自由度
blocks.translation: Freedom of Choice

blocks.source: https://newrpg.seesaa.net/article/377351764.html
blocks.translation: https://newrpg.seesaa.net/article/377351764.html

blocks.source: なお、必ずしも無理にそのような要素を盛り込む必要はない。
blocks.translation: That said, you do not necessarily need to force such elements into your game.

blocks.source: ストーリー分岐があると周回プレイが前提になりがちだが、ゲーム部分は大半が同じなので飽きやすくなってしまう。サブクエストは基本的に寄り道なので、メインストーリーのテンポが悪化する。
blocks.translation: Story branches tend to make repeated playthroughs necessary, but most of the gameplay remains the same, making it easy for players to lose interest. Side quests are essentially detours, so they can disrupt the pacing of the main story.

blocks.source: メインストーリーに注力するから分岐やサブクエストは必要ない――というのも立派な判断だ。
blocks.translation: Choosing not to include branches or side quests in order to focus on the main story is also a perfectly valid decision.

blocks.source: 目的は明確に
blocks.translation: Make the Objective Clear

blocks.source: 次にどこへ行けばいいのか分からないシナリオは、プレイヤーを困惑させやすい。
blocks.translation: A scenario in which players do not know where to go next can easily leave them confused.

blocks.source: 現代のＲＰＧではメインストーリーで行き先を明示するのが大半だ。もちろん町人との会話など、プレイヤーが自発的に情報収集することをも求めてもよい。
blocks.translation: In most modern RPGs, the main story clearly indicates where to go. Of course, you can also ask players to gather information on their own by talking with townspeople and so on.

blocks.source: どちらの方針を取るにせよ、何も考えなかった結果、単なる不親切になったという状況は避けたい。
blocks.translation: Whichever approach you take, you should avoid ending up with a situation where a lack of thought simply makes the game feel unfriendly.

blocks.source: 以下はありがちな不親切である。
blocks.translation: The following are common examples of being unfriendly to the player.

blocks.source: 目的地の名前は明示していても、肝心の場所がノーヒント。
blocks.translation: The destination is named, but there are no clues as to where it actually is.

blocks.source: メインストーリー上の説明を見落とすと、以降説明が読めなくなる。
blocks.translation: If the player misses an explanation in the main story, no further explanations can be read.

blocks.source: 今時の作品は、システムの機能で目的地を知らせてくれるものが多い。メニュー画面のあらすじやクエスト一覧などが一般的だろう。
blocks.translation: Many modern games use system features to inform players of their objectives. A summary of the story or a quest list in the menu is common.

blocks.source: エンディング
blocks.translation: Ending

blocks.source: 特にこだわりがないなら、ゲームのエンディングはハッピーエンドを用意すべきだと考えている。
blocks.translation: Unless you have a particular reason not to, I believe games should have a happy ending.

blocks.source: 小説などの他媒体でも、基本的にハッピーエンドのほうが無難だと思うが、ゲームは特にその必要性が高い。
blocks.translation: Happy endings are generally the safer choice in other media, such as novels, but they are especially important in games.

blocks.source: というのも、プレイヤーに労力を要求する点が、ゲームと他の媒体との決定的な違いだからだ。
blocks.translation: That is because requiring effort from the player is a decisive difference between games and other forms of media.

blocks.source: そして「プレイヤーの操作によって困難に打ち勝つ」のがゲームの基本構造であるため、「どうあがいても絶望」というのは、それに反してしまう。
blocks.translation: Since the basic structure of a game is to “overcome difficulties through the player’s actions,” a situation of “despair no matter what you do” goes against that structure.

blocks.source: 何十時間も苦労した上で強制バッドエンドを見せられるのは、プレイヤーにとって相当な苦痛となってしまうだろう。
blocks.translation: Being forced to watch a bad ending after struggling for dozens of hours would be extremely painful for the player.

blocks.source: もちろん、選択次第でバッドエンドになるような要素もあってよい。バッドがあってこそ、ハッピーが際立つという考えもある。
blocks.translation: Of course, it is fine to include elements that lead to a bad ending depending on the player’s choices. Some believe that happy endings stand out more because bad endings exist.

blocks.source: ただし、長いプレイ時間が無に帰すような仕組みはやめたほうがいい。
blocks.translation: However, you should avoid systems that render many hours of play meaningless.

blocks.source: 酷い例としてはペルソナ１が有名だろう。
blocks.translation: Persona 1 is probably a well-known example of a particularly bad case.

blocks.source: このゲームは途中の選択肢を誤ると、バッドエンドに分岐して物語の途中で終了してしまう。取り返しは一切つかない。
blocks.translation: In this game, choosing the wrong option along the way branches into a bad ending and abruptly ends the story. There is no way to undo it.

blocks.source: 分岐点まで普通にやると５０時間程度かかるので、当時何人ものプレイヤーが心を折られた。……というか、エンディング分岐があると気づかないままゲームを終えたプレイヤーもいたとか。
blocks.translation: Playing normally up to the branching point takes about 50 hours, so many players at the time were utterly disheartened. In fact, some players reportedly finished the game without realizing that the endings could branch.

blocks.source: 直前でもフラグを満たせばハッピ―に分岐できるとか、短～中編で最初からやり直してもそこまで苦にならないとか、バッドを見るとすぐに分岐からやり直せるとか、何らかの配慮が欲しい。
blocks.translation: Some consideration is needed, such as allowing players to branch to the happy ending by fulfilling the requirements right before the ending, making the game short or medium-length so restarting from the beginning is not too burdensome, or allowing them to immediately retry from the branch after viewing a bad ending.

blocks.source: 主人公の活躍
blocks.translation: The Protagonist’s Achievements

blocks.source: ＲＰＧの多くは基本的に主人公（＝プレイヤー）を中心とした一人称の物語である。ゆえに、その物語も主人公を中心とすることが望ましい。きちんと活躍の機会を設けてあげよう。
blocks.translation: Most RPGs are essentially first-person stories centered on the protagonist (= the player). Therefore, the story should also center on the protagonist. Be sure to give them opportunities to shine.

blocks.source: ※群像劇など、特定の主人公を定めない作品もあります。
blocks.translation: ※Some works, such as ensemble dramas, do not establish a specific protagonist.

blocks.source: 無口主人公
blocks.translation: The Silent Protagonist

blocks.source: 注意が必要なのは無口主人公を採用した場合だ。
blocks.translation: You need to be careful when choosing to use a silent protagonist.

blocks.source: ゲーム以外の媒体では、まず見ることのないタイプの主人公だが、その扱いは意外と難しい。
blocks.translation: This type of protagonist is rarely seen outside of games, but handling one is surprisingly difficult.

blocks.source: 特に仲間がよく喋る作品だと、主人公の存在が希薄になりやすい。仲間同士の会話中心で物語が進んでしまうと、主人公が何のためにいるのか存在価値が疑わしくなってしまう。
blocks.translation: The protagonist’s presence is especially likely to fade in works where the party members talk a lot. If the story progresses mainly through conversations between party members, it becomes questionable why the protagonist is there and what value they have.

blocks.source: これについては、以下の記事で書いているので割愛。
blocks.translation: I have written about this in the following article, so I will omit it here.

blocks.source: 無口主人公の考察
blocks.translation: Thoughts on Silent Protagonists

blocks.source: https://newrpg.seesaa.net/article/295119708.html
blocks.translation: https://newrpg.seesaa.net/article/295119708.html

blocks.source: 主人公の能動性
blocks.translation: The Protagonist’s Initiative

blocks.source: 意外とありがちなのは、敵の思惑やその場の状況に振り回されているばかりで、主人公達が能動的に行動していないというケース。
blocks.translation: A surprisingly common case is one where the protagonists merely get pushed around by the enemy’s schemes and the situation at hand, without taking any initiative themselves.

blocks.source: ゲームである以上、主人公が自らの意思で目的へ向かっているという感触は欲しい。
blocks.translation: Since this is a game, players should feel that the protagonist is pursuing their goal of their own free will.

blocks.source: 主人公（＝プレイヤー）の行動によって、事態を改善しているという実感が得られないようでは達成感が乏しくなってしまう。
blocks.translation: If players cannot feel that the protagonist (= the player) is improving the situation through their actions, the sense of achievement will be diminished.

blocks.source: 成功体験
blocks.translation: A Sense of Accomplishment

blocks.source: もっと言うと、プレイヤーにははっきりと成功体験を与えてあげよう。
blocks.translation: In other words, you should give players a clear sense of accomplishment.

blocks.source: 悪役の撃破
blocks.translation: Defeating the Villain

blocks.source: 目的の達成
blocks.translation: Achieving the objective

blocks.source: ヒロインや仲間からの信頼獲得
blocks.translation: Earning the trust of the heroine and companions

blocks.source: 当たり前のことなのだが、こういった当たり前がおろそかになる作品は珍しくない。
blocks.translation: This may seem obvious, but works in which such obvious things are neglected are not uncommon.

blocks.source: 倒しても倒しても、ボスが余裕綽々で去っていくので勝った気がしない。
blocks.translation: No matter how many times you defeat the boss, they leave in complete composure, so it never feels like you won.

blocks.source: 状況に振り回されるばかりで、気づいてみれば何も成し遂げていない。
blocks.translation: You are merely swept along by circumstances, and before you know it, you have accomplished nothing.

blocks.source: 何をやっても裏目に出て失敗続き。
blocks.translation: Everything you do backfires, and you suffer one failure after another.

blocks.source: ストーリー後半になっても、パーティがギスギスしている。
blocks.translation: Even in the latter half of the story, the party is still at odds.

blocks.source: ていうか、ヒロインが他の男とくっついた。
blocks.translation: Actually, the heroine ended up with another guy.

blocks.source: 上記のような作品に遭遇した経験のある人もいるかと思う。
blocks.translation: Some of you may have encountered works like those described above.

blocks.source: このような例はむしろ、ストーリー性の高い作品で遭遇しやすい印象すらある。話に凝りすぎたばかりに、基本がおろそかになっているのかもしれない。
blocks.translation: In fact, I even get the impression that these examples are more common in story-driven works. Perhaps the basics are neglected because too much attention is devoted to the plot.

blocks.source: なお、この反対の失敗体験が駄目なわけではない。
blocks.translation: That said, the opposite kind of failure is not necessarily a bad experience.

blocks.source: むしろ、アクセント的に失敗を入れたほうが成功は際立つ。特に序盤で急激に落として、そこから盛り上げていくようなストーリー構成は定番だと言えるだろう。
blocks.translation: Rather, including failures as accents can make the successes stand out more. In particular, a story structure that takes a sharp turn downward early on and then builds back up from there could be called a classic.

texts.小説、映画、漫画、アニメ……ストーリー性を持った媒体は様々に存在するが、ゲームも: Novels, films, manga, anime... There are many forms of media with stories, and games are one of them.
texts.ゲームにもＲＰＧ、シミュレーション、アクション、ＡＤＶというように様々なジャンル: Games also come in many genres, such as RPGs, simulations, action games, and ADV games.
texts.シナリオは媒体やジャンルによって、最適なものを書く必要がある。: A scenario needs to be tailored to its medium and genre.
texts.というわけで、ＲＰＧのゲーム性を意識した上で、どのようなシナリオを書けばよいかを: With that in mind, I would like to consider what kind of scenario to write while keeping the gameplay of an RPG in mind.
texts.逆に「シナリオを活かすために、どのようなシステムを用意すればいいか」という観点も: Conversely, I have also written about what kinds of systems should be prepared to make the most of a scenario.
texts.筆者は個人制作者なので、もちろんゲームデザイナー兼シナリオライターという立場であ: As an independent creator, I naturally fill the roles of both game designer and scenario writer.
texts.現代のプロのゲームクリエイターは専門化されていて、両方に精通している人は希少らし: Modern professional game creators tend to specialize, and apparently it is rare to find someone well versed in both areas. I hope to offer perspectives that can only be gained by someone who does both.
texts.そのまま個人制作で活かしてもいいし。ゲームデザイナーとシナリオライターで分業する: You can apply these ideas directly to your own solo projects, or use them as points to keep in mind when dividing the work between a game designer and a scenario writer.
texts.なお、過去にも以下のような記事を書いているが、今回はより詳細に掘り下げている。: I have written articles like the following in the past, but this time I delve into the subject in greater detail.
texts.ＲＰＧのシナリオを考える上で、まず大事なのは仲間の存在である。: When considering an RPG scenario, the first important thing is the presence of companions.
texts.多くのＲＰＧでは主人公は数多くの仲間を引き連れて、冒険することになる。: In many RPGs, the protagonist goes on adventures accompanied by numerous companions.
texts.仲間はプレイヤーにとって、ゲームシステム上の駒である。だが、そこにストーリー性が: To the player, companions are pieces within the game system. However, when they are tied to the story, they can become more than mere pieces.
texts.魅力的な仲間達を操作できるということは、ＲＰＧの大きな魅力だ。これを活かさない手: Being able to control appealing companions is one of the great attractions of RPGs. There is no reason not to make use of it.
texts.仲間の加入はストーリー的にもゲーム的にも、大きな見所となる。魅力的なキャラクター: A companion joining the party is a major highlight, both in terms of the story and the gameplay. When an appealing character joins the party, it should bring the player great joy as well.
texts.さらには、加入した仲間が戦闘でも大活躍できる性能だった時は、大いに盛り上がるだろ: Furthermore, if the new companion proves highly effective in battle, it will make the experience even more exciting.
texts.そんなわけで、ゲーム序盤は仲間の加入イベントを用意するのがセオリーとなる。: For this reason, preparing companion recruitment events early in the game is standard practice.
texts.ヒロインとの運命の出会いや、頼りになる相棒との出会いを、華々しく演出しよう。: Dramatically portray the fateful meeting with the heroine or the encounter with a dependable partner.
texts.活躍機会を与えるためにも、仲間の加入は遅すぎないほうが望ましい。中盤ぐらいまでに: To give companions opportunities to shine, it is preferable not to have them join too late. A good guideline might be to have most of the characters available by around the midpoint.
texts.特に注意したいのは序盤の仲間の加入だ。: The companions who join early in the game require particular attention.
texts.多くのＲＰＧでは一人旅を含めた少人数では、取れる戦術が限られてしまう。: In many RPGs, when the party is small, including when traveling alone, the tactics available to the player become limited.
texts.その中でも、回復役がいない状況がずっと続くのは厳しい。回復役は比較的、早めに加入: In particular, it is difficult if the party goes too long without a healer. Have a healer join relatively early. Another standard approach, as seen in the Dragon Quest series, is to have the protagonist learn some healing Techs.
texts.なお、ポケモンのように回復技を前提としたゲームバランスになっていない作品はこの限: This does not apply to games such as Pokémon, whose game balance is not built around the use of healing Techs.
texts.その他の仲間についても、ゲーム性に合わせて調整したい。: The other companions should also be adjusted to fit the gameplay.
texts.例えば、通常攻撃しかできない少人数の旅がずっと続いてしまうと、プレイヤーも退屈に: For example, if the player spends too long traveling with a small party that can only use normal attacks, they will become bored. Have a companion with skills that expand their tactical options, such as magic, join early on.
texts.仲間は徐々に増やす: Increase the Number of Companions Gradually
texts.ならば、冒頭から大勢の仲間を加入させてはどうか？: In that case, why not have a large number of companions join right from the beginning?
texts.……と、思うかもしれないが、そちらも避けたほうが無難だろう。: You might think so, but it would probably be safer to avoid that as well.
texts.というのも、一人一人に焦点を当てる機会が減るので、プレイヤーがキャラクターを把握: The reason is that there will be fewer opportunities to focus on each individual, making it harder for players to get to know the characters.
texts.また、システム的にもいきなり大勢の仲間を管理する必要が出るので、慣れない内からプ: From a systems perspective, the player would also suddenly have to manage a large number of companions, increasing the burden before they have had time to get used to the game.
texts.単純にストーリーのネタが減ってしまうのも厳しい。仲間の登場と加入のイベントはそれ: It is also difficult simply because it reduces the amount of story material available. Events involving the appearance and recruitment of companions are powerful hooks in themselves, so I think it would be a waste not to use them.
texts.もっとも、この辺は作品の狙いによって様々なやり方があるので、柔軟に考えて欲しい。: That said, there are many possible approaches depending on the goals of the work, so I hope you will think flexibly.
texts.例えば、冒頭からいきなり多人数パーティにした代わりに、徐々に仲間を掘り下げていく: For example, one possible style is to start with a large party and gradually delve deeper into each companion instead.
texts.成長・強化システムと仲間の加入・離脱には相性がある。ストーリーを作成する上で無視: Growth and enhancement systems have a natural compatibility with companions joining and leaving the party. This is an aspect that cannot be ignored when creating a story.
texts.これについては、過去の記事でも詳しく書いている。: I wrote about this in detail in a previous article as well.
texts.例えば、ドラクエ６～７の職業システムが有名だろう。: For example, the class systems in Dragon Quest VI and VII are probably well known.
texts.両作品の職業は戦闘回数によって、呪文・特技を習得するようになっている。: In both games, characters learn spells and Techs for their classes based on the number of battles fought.
texts.後半、仲間になったキャラは職業の初期レベルが固定になっており、扱いづらくなってし: Characters who join later in the game have fixed starting levels for their classes, which makes them more difficult to use.
texts.また、レベルアップボーナスのようなシステムがある作品だと、後半に高レベルで仲間に: Also, in games with systems such as level-up bonuses, characters who join at high levels later in the game tend to be disadvantaged.
texts.このようなシステムはそもそも採用しないほうが無難だろう。: It would probably be safer not to use such a system in the first place.
texts.逆に言うと昔のドラクエのように、レベルと装備だけで能力が決まるような単純な設計な: Conversely, with a simple design like that of the older Dragon Quest games, where abilities are determined solely by level and equipment, having a character join late does not cause any major problems.
texts.あるいはドラクエ８や１１のように、ポイント振り分け型のシステムも問題は起きにくい: Alternatively, point-allocation systems like those in Dragon Quest VIII and XI are also less likely to cause problems. You can simply allow players to freely allocate points after a character joins.
texts.ただし、あまりにも振り分けに時間がかかるようなシステムだと、プレイヤーの手間が増: However, keep in mind that if the system takes too much time to allocate points, it will increase the player's workload.
texts.ストーリー上の都合で、頻繁にパーティ編成を変えてしまうと、結果的にシステムを十分: When the party lineup is changed frequently for story-related reasons, the player ultimately cannot fully experience the system (as in the first half of FF XIII, for example).
texts.さらに厳しいのは仲間の永久離脱だ。: Even harsher is when companions leave the party permanently.
texts.成長システムが凝ったものになればなるほど、仲間の離脱は好まれなくなる。せっかく手: The more elaborate the growth system becomes, the less welcome it is for companions to leave. After taking the trouble to raise someone, it is only natural to feel frustrated when they leave for story-related reasons.
texts.こういった作品の場合は、ゲームシステムの段階でフォローをしておきたい。: For works like these, I want the game system itself to provide some support.
texts.ＦＦ５では離脱した仲間の能力を引き継いだ後継キャラが加入する。: In FF V, a successor character who inherits the abilities of a departed companion joins the party.
texts.ＦＦ７ではマテリアシステムによって、モノを成長させる仕様になっており、離脱による: In FF VII, the Materia system is designed around developing items, so the loss of combat power caused by a companion's departure is less painful.
texts.仲間の人数が多い作品は、単純に管理の手間が増えるため、複雑な成長・強化システムと: Works with many companions are a poor match for complex growth and enhancement systems, simply because they require more effort to manage.
texts.例えば、軌跡シリーズには数十人という膨大な仲間が登場する作品もある。それらがスト: For example, some entries in the Trails series feature a huge number of companions—dozens of them. They join and leave according to the story, and each time, you have to rearrange a large number of pieces of equipment.
texts.場合によっては、パーティ分割ダンジョンなどで１２人以上の装備を整える必要があった: In some cases, such as dungeons that split the party, you may need to prepare equipment for more than twelve characters. This creates a level of stress that players cannot simply ignore.
texts.仲間になる人数が多い作品でも、戦闘に参加する人数が少なく、限られたキャラだけを整: Even in works with many recruitable companions, the burden can be reduced if only a small number participate in battle and you only need to prepare a limited selection of characters.
texts.無理に大勢の仲間を使わせるようなストーリーおよびシステムを作ると、それだけ手間が: Keep in mind that creating a story and system that force players to use a large number of companions will require a corresponding amount of extra work.
texts.かわいい子には旅を: Send Your Beloved Child on a Journey
texts.仲間として旅に参加するキャラクターは、ゲーム的にもシナリオ的にも出番がとても多く: Characters who join the journey as companions get far more screen time, both in terms of gameplay and the story.
texts.故郷で主人公の帰りを待つヒロインと、主人公と共に戦うヒロインならば、後者のほうが: Between a heroine who waits in her hometown for the protagonist to return and one who fights alongside the protagonist, the latter will surely inspire far more attachment.
texts.漫画やアニメ、ＡＤＶならば、「戦士として敵と戦う主人公」の裏で「王女として政治に: In manga, anime, or an ADV, you could make a heroine who busies herself with politics as a princess plenty appealing while the protagonist fights enemies as a warrior. In an RPG, however, this is also difficult.
texts.ＲＰＧでは、プレイ時間の大半が主人公の周辺の出来事として描かれるためだ。特に戦闘: That is because most of an RPG's playtime depicts events taking place around the protagonist. Combat and exploration, in particular, make up a large portion of it.
texts.それらの際に、主人公に同行していないヒロインは圧倒的に描写が不足してしまう。同行: During those parts, a heroine who does not accompany the protagonist ends up being dramatically underrepresented. Compared with an accompanying heroine, the difference in the amount of time players see her can even exceed a hundredfold.
texts.ヒロインは主人公の幼馴染で小さい頃からずっと仲良くしていた――なんて説明をされた: You can explain that the heroine is the protagonist's childhood friend and that they have been close since they were young—but the player did not share those experiences, so there is only so much that can be done.
texts.ヒロインを例に挙げたけど、他のキャラクターも同様である。: I used the heroine as an example, but the same applies to other characters.
texts.敵キャラならば、実際に何度も戦って苦戦した相手のほうが印象も強くなる。: For an enemy, one that players have actually fought repeatedly and struggled against will leave a much stronger impression.
texts.キャラクターの印象を強くしたいなら、ゲームシステム上の出番を用意してあげよう。: If you want to make a character more memorable, give them opportunities to appear through the game system.
texts.一般的なＲＰＧでは戦闘がゲーム性の肝になる。: In a typical RPG, combat is the core of the gameplay.
texts.ＲＰＧのゲーム性とは事実上戦闘であり、それを意識せずしてストーリーは作れない。必: In practice, an RPG's gameplay is combat, and it is impossible to create a story without taking that into account. Inevitably, the story must also be designed with combat in mind.
texts.※戦闘のないＲＰＧのようなごくわずかの例外もありますが、今回は置いておきます。: ※There are a very few exceptions, such as RPGs without combat, but we will set those aside for now.
texts.ストーリーとゲーム性の一致: Aligning the Story with the Gameplay
texts.例えば、戦いを否定する平和主義的なストーリーを作りたいとしよう。主人公やヒロイン: For example, suppose you want to create a pacifist story that rejects fighting. The protagonist and heroine relentlessly denounce violence and continue seeking dialogue with their enemies.
texts.このようなストーリーのコンセプトと、ひたすら敵を倒すことを要求するゲームシステム: I think it is intuitively clear that this story concept is a poor match for a game system that relentlessly demands that players defeat enemies.
texts.綺麗事を言っていても、結局は戦闘で物事を解決するならば、どこか偽善的な印象をプレ: Even if the characters talk about lofty ideals, if they ultimately solve everything through combat, players will be left with a somewhat hypocritical impression.
texts.ならば――と、戦闘の回避を推奨するようなシステムを導入してしまうと、今度は戦闘シ: You might then introduce a system that encourages avoiding combat, but that would eliminate the point of creating an elaborate combat system in the first place.
texts.そんなわけで、オーソドックスにＲＰＧを作るならば、ストーリーは戦いを前提にするこ: Therefore, if you are making a conventional RPG, it is probably safest for the story to be built around conflict.
texts.多くのＲＰＧではボスを倒すことが物語の目的に直結している。: In many RPGs, defeating the boss is directly tied to the story's objective.
texts.ボスには中ボスからラスボスまで色々とあるが、ボス戦こそがＲＰＧの華だと言ってもよ: There are various kinds of bosses, from mid-bosses to the final boss, but it would not be an exaggeration to say that boss battles are the highlight of an RPG.
texts.従って、ＲＰＧのストーリーもボス戦を意識して作成することが望ましい。: Accordingly, it is best to create an RPG story with boss battles in mind.
texts.そのためにも、必要なのは魅力的な敵キャラだ。: To that end, what you need are compelling enemies.
texts.非道な悪党でも、悲劇の悪役でも、正々堂々としたライバルでもいい。魅力の出し方は様: They can be a ruthless villain, a tragic antagonist, or an honorable rival. There are many ways to make an enemy compelling.
texts.ベタではあるが『四天王』のような敵幹部を用意するのも王道だ。: It may be a cliché, but creating a group of enemy commanders like the Four Heavenly Kings is also a classic approach.
texts.敵キャラには出番と対決の機会が欠かせない。顔見せ的なイベントを作ったり、複数回の: Enemies need opportunities to appear and chances to face the player. Create introductory events, provide multiple opportunities for confrontation, and work to make them more memorable.
texts.こういったストーリー上の宿敵との激戦は、ゲームでしか得られない熱さがある。: Fierce battles against story-defining nemeses like these have an intensity that can only be experienced in a game.
texts.ありがちなのは、各エリアの最後にその場限りのボスが現れるばかりというパターン。そ: A common pattern is for a disposable boss to appear at the end of each area and nowhere else. To avoid that, give careful thought to how you portray your enemies.
texts.ゲームである以上、プレイヤーが操作する戦闘は大切であり、尊重しなければならない。: Since this is a game, the combat controlled by the player is important and must be respected. It is best to avoid developments that disregard the player's input for the sake of the story.
texts.プレイヤーが戦闘でボスを倒しても、ボスがピンピンしてるパターン。: This is the pattern where the player defeats a boss in battle, yet the boss is still perfectly fine.
texts.「なかなかやるな。今日はここまでにしよう」などと宣って、ボスは颯爽と去っていく。: The boss declares something like, “Not bad. Let's call it a day,” then makes a dramatic exit. It is a scene we have seen countless times in works such as Trails of Cold Steel.
texts.一度の戦闘だけで決着をつけてしまうと、敵キャラの掘り下げができないため、ある程度: It is somewhat unavoidable, since resolving everything in a single battle would leave no opportunity to develop the enemy character.
texts.とはいえ、このような展開は「プレイヤーが勝利した」という達成感を損ねてしまう。こ: Even so, developments like these undermine the feeling of accomplishment that comes from “the player achieving victory.” If this happens too often, battles increasingly start to feel like a farce, which is unlikely to leave players feeling good.
texts.ゼノブレイド２～３では、プレイヤーが介入できない戦闘ムービーが非常に多い。: In Xenoblade Chronicles 2 and 3, there are an enormous number of battle cutscenes in which the player cannot intervene.
texts.プレイヤーが戦闘でボスを倒したのにも関わらず、それがなかったかのように長い戦闘ム: Even when the player has defeated a boss in battle, a lengthy battle cutscene is inserted as if that had never happened. With flashy effects impossible to achieve on the regular battle screen, these scenes greatly heighten the excitement of the enemy's defeat.
texts.……が、その一方で、プレイヤーの操作する戦闘は、シーンの合間に挟まれるミニゲーム: ...On the other hand, the battles controlled by the player are like minigames inserted between scenes. Personally, they even left me thinking, “Do we really need player input?” and “Wouldn’t it be better to just watch an anime?”
texts.こういった問題は戦闘とムービーの落差を小さくすれば、ある程度は違和感を抑えられる: I think these issues can be made less jarring by reducing the gap between battles and cutscenes to some extent. For example, the finishing sequence could be presented as an extension of the battle.
texts.イベントバトルの功罪: The Merits and Demerits of Event Battles
texts.強制敗北戦闘や強制勝利戦闘といったイベントバトルは、ＲＰＧの定番である。: Event battles, such as forced-loss battles and forced-win battles, are staples of RPGs.
texts.例えば、圧倒的な強さを持ったボスに強制敗北させることで、将来の再戦への期待を持た: For example, forcing the player to lose to an overwhelmingly powerful boss can build anticipation for a rematch in the future.
texts.ドラクエ５における少年期の最後のシーンは有名だが、強く印象に残った人も多いだろう: The final scene of the childhood arc in Dragon Quest V is famous, and many people probably remember it vividly.
